# Risks

None to runtime code: only `packages/app-core/scripts/run-node-supervisor.test.mjs` changes. Failure mode changes from a 30s vitest timeout plus an uncaught ENOENT to an immediate rejection carrying the supervisor's captured stderr.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`runSupervisor()`'s `child.on("exit")` handler read the fake child's `spawn-count.txt` unguarded. When the supervisor aborts before spawning (the Windows-runner failure mode in #18512), the file does not exist, the read throws inside an EventEmitter callback, the promise never settles, and both tests burn the 30s timeout while the one line saying what went wrong (supervisor stderr) is discarded. The exit handler now guards the read and rejects immediately with the exit code and captured stderr.

This carries the original fix from #18519 (author @felirami, commit preserved) minus the extracted helper module + helper unit tests: an 83-line scaffold around a 10-line guard on the test harness itself. Net diff is one test file, +19/−4.

# Risks

**Large.** This changes Google OAuth secret handling, agent authorization, connector migration, runtime tool materialization, and the execution protocol for personal Gmail/Calendar/Drive/Docs/Sheets/Slides/People/Chat/Search. The main mitigations are vault-only durable secrets, per-call binding/scope rechecks, curated exact tool allowlists, fail-closed unsupported operations, a sole-agent-only migration backfill, and explicit multi-agent rebinding.

Google Workspace MCP remains Developer Preview. Gmail is intentionally draft-only because the official server has no send tool. Calendar is intentionally read-only because current MCP event schemas do not provide the idempotency and atomic version preconditions required by existing LifeOps write guarantees.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds a stateless MCP v2 remote-resource engine with exact calls, pagination, SSRF validation, opaque attachment generations, and injected short-lived access-token providers.
- Replaces personal Google REST execution with Google's official per-product MCP endpoints.
- Uses one direct authorization-code OAuth flow. OAuth app secrets, refresh/access tokens, and PKCE verifiers are stored behind vault/secret references; raw refresh tokens are not serialized into MCP config.
- Separates a reusable OAuth account from per-agent bindings. Bindings own selected products, allowed capabilities, default selection, status, and independent revocation.
- Dynamically materializes only reviewed namespaced tools and removes them when a product, capability, scope, binding, or connection is removed.
- Makes Cloud call official Google resources directly from its trusted runtime and revalidates the current binding, product, capability, tool, and scopes before bearer injection. The old Google broker/stub routes are removed.
- Thins `plugin-google-workspace` to OAuth, vault resolution, the multi-resource capability host, stable typed adapters, and the separate service-account Google Chat connector.
- Removes personal Google REST clients, Calendar watch/webhook infrastructure, Meet REST artifacts, Gmail Watch registry data, legacy Mockoon/REST fixtures, and old Gmail compatibility scenario contracts.
- Migrates Gmail/Calendar scenarios to deterministic MCP fixtures and exact call ledgers. Unsupported spam/bulk/send/calendar-write behavior is asserted to fail closed.
- Regenerates Cloud routes/SDK wrappers and the first-party plugin registry.

This PR completes the personal Google Workspace MCP-only cutover. It does not implement the broader Linear/Notion/GitHub SaaS deletion wave from the long-term portfolio plan.

## What kind of change is this?

Features, improvements, security hardening, database migration, and intentional removal of obsolete connector compatibility surfaces.

# Documentation changes needed?

Documentation was updated for the direct OAuth/vault/binding model, official MCP endpoints, draft-only Gmail, read-only Calendar, removed broker/watch/mock surfaces, and the service-account Chat exception.

## What changed

- makes first contact and Steward sign-in resolve one persistent personal Eliza identity across phone, web, desktop, and native clients
- adds rowless account-scoped Shared chat with durable transcript/idempotency, metered search, credit-gated voice, and deterministic capability walls
- removes automatic signup credits and every implicit paid-compute/provisioning path in this product journey
- adds explicit Dedicated quote/confirm/cancel, singleton provisioning, authoritative sealing, and atomic Shared-to-Dedicated cutover
- replaces the generic agent dashboard with a compact personal-Eliza cockpit while preserving balance and account controls
- restores and polishes the phone-first landing page, including one-viewport responsive geometry from 320x568 through desktop

## Why

The existing product mixed generic hosted-agent provisioning with the personal-assistant entrypoint. That created paid rows before consent, fragmented identity across phone and app, and made Shared appear capable of actions it could not safely perform. This change gives the product one identity authority, one free Shared service boundary, and one explicit paid upgrade boundary.

- personal lifecycle focused matrix: 257 checks
- first-run no-auto-provision: 33/33

This refactor makes the personal Shared agent run the canonical edge Todo plugin, persists Todo mutations exactly once, and carries Todo rows plus replay authority through identity convergence and Shared-to-Dedicated cutover.

## Scope

- Run `@elizaos/plugin-todos/edge` inside the genuine Shared `AgentRuntime`.
- Store Todos and immutable mutation receipts in control-plane Postgres with tenant-qualified scopes.
- Replay a repeated keyed mutation as the original no-op receipt; reject changed semantics under the same key.
- Preserve Todo IDs, parent links, mutation IDs, receipt IDs, and replay authority during phone-to-Telegram convergence and Shared-to-Dedicated cutover.
- Keep reminder delivery on the scheduling subsystem; Todos do not create a second scheduler.
- Publish a UI-free Node/Worker package contract and build every imported edge dependency before Cloud shared typecheck.

## Final merged candidate

Final PR head: `db1701c3d336eaeb30a38083ad492888a98ba324`  
Merge commit: `d4845d272c16e65a39433ad3ebe92799afeadfcf`  
Final base: `origin/develop@e65ce00a2e33ae46ebdad6eae36115162aebf6e2`  
Shared final tree: `0f14ad87ecb6fe9e677d9e114230701e3df1c47c`

- JSON-RPC IDs are connection-local correlation only. Unkeyed calls receive fresh durable message IDs, so a restarted counter cannot replay an old Todo mutation. Keyed calls derive stable durable identities from `clientMessageId`.
- Shared Todo migrations follow develop's `0205_identity_links_transport_source`: `0206_shared_todos.sql` and `0207_todo_mutation_ledger.sql`.
- The packed edge-export contract permits a real clean package build instead of failing on a CI-speed assumption.
- Turbo builds scheduling, Todos, and web-search edge dependencies before `@elizaos/cloud-shared#typecheck`, removing clean-run ordering races.

Shaw rebased and merged the reviewed series. Independent post-merge audit found all **35/35** reviewed patches range-diff equivalent. All Todo migration and journal blobs are byte-identical to the reviewed candidate and ordered after `0205` as `0206` and `0207`.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds a stateless exact-call MCP resource engine with guarded fetches, paginated discovery, generation-safe attachment handles, short-lived access-token callbacks, bounded requests, and no persisted bearer headers.
- Extends connector accounts with agent, owner, OAuth mode, execution-target, selected-product, scope, and capability contracts; adds durable Cloud agent-connector bindings and revocation behavior.
- Materializes only two curated Google actions when compatible tools are discovered: `GOOGLE_GMAIL_SEARCH_THREADS` and `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_LIST_EVENTS`.
- Makes typed Calendar list reads MCP-first with an observable direct-API fallback while retaining direct APIs for writes, Gmail send, Chat bot, and Meet behavior.
- Adds a Mode A Cloud broker that resolves the exact agent binding and private credential, mints a short-lived access token, targets fixed official Google product endpoints, and enforces product/tool allowlists.
- Replaces the singular `/api/mcps/google` stub with per-agent, per-binding, per-product routes and preserves lean-chat/mobile gating.
- Adds the shared official Google product endpoint catalog and coverage tests.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature: a production-shaped MCP-first connector control-plane slice that reduces future vendor-client ownership without deleting the stable LifeOps service seam.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Runs free rowless Shared turns through a genuine elizaOS `AgentRuntime` inside Cloudflare Workerd instead of a bare prompt/model shim.
- Adds a minimal edge-safe plugin set: canonical keyless web search and reminders.
- Keeps ordered conversation/replay state in Durable Objects and multi-tenant scheduled-task/account state in Postgres through Hyperdrive.
- Uses Cloudflare cron to claim due reminders and the existing Railway gateway for one idempotent Telegram egress.
- Transfers canonical chat history and reminder/task identity/state to Dedicated using a two-phase reserve/import/activate/retire protocol.
- Preserves Shaw's current phone, Telegram, Discord, voice, lifecycle-system-message, and cross-channel continuity changes.
- Keeps Shared rowless and platform-funded: no automatic agent row, credit grant, container, or paid compute.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature plus correctness hardening.

## Outcome

This restores the managed dedicated-agent **Open → pair → authenticated app** path and closes the credential-boundary holes found while tracing the original “expired link” failure.

- The Hetzner router preserves the Worker-pinned public agent host instead of replacing it with the control-plane host.
- Managed pairing terminates at the Cloud Worker, claims the one-time token atomically against the exact agent and origin, and writes only an owner-scoped browser credential.
- Remote containers cannot re-enable the direct pairing relay; local Docker retains an explicit loopback-only compatibility mode.
- Pre-auth managed HTML never contains the full agent bearer.
- The dedicated-agent proxy strips Cloud cookies/credential headers, rejects authenticated non-owners, owns CORS, strips response cookies/site-clearing headers, preserves WebSocket upgrades, and removes every Cloud-shaped realtime query credential before forwarding.
- UI restore/switch paths bind credentials to UUID agent owners and trusted bases, use an atomic base+token WebSocket repoint, never send Steward credentials to loopback, and make profile persistence failure visible instead of reporting a false successful switch.

79:T1b9c,## Authority decision

This draft supersedes #17462 as the controlled integration branch. Exact comparison found that neither #17462 at `fd22d142b28c` nor this branch's earlier `8cfdca706ba` was independently safe: both copied Slack credentials into plain Character settings, and #17462 also carried a second, divergent policy implementation and stale evidence. This branch now has one authority, `plugins/plugin-slack/src/policy.ts`; there is no parallel `allowlist.ts` engine.

The branch remains draft. Do not merge until live sandbox Slack evidence and independent exact-head review are complete.

## Repair

- Splits canonical `config.connectors.slack` at the runtime boundary. Non-secret policy reaches `character.settings.slack`; top-level and per-account `botToken`, `appToken`, `userToken`, and `signingSecret` exist only in `character.secrets.SLACK_CONNECTOR_CREDENTIALS_JSON` and are strictly parsed as credentials.
- Proves credential-bearing fields and values are absent from serialized plain settings while canonical policy still reaches account startup.
- Preserves env-only compatibility without accidentally materializing structured policy. Canonical persisted schema defaults intentionally select strict `groupPolicy: allowlist`; env-only boot retains its historical message/channel behavior.
- Compiles one account-scoped policy before Bolt starts. Channel and user names resolve to immutable IDs with pagination, ambiguity, inactive-user, and unresolved-name failures. Explicit opaque IDs use `id:` or `slack-id:` and do not depend on Slack prefix conventions.
- Requires authenticated bot and workspace identity, isolates accounts/workspaces, and rejects missing or foreign attribution across message, app mention, reaction, join/leave, and file event families.
- Classifies public/private channels, DMs, App Home, MPIMs, and threads through API/event metadata; enforces group, channel, user, bot, mention, DM, pairing, and group-DM policy without dynamic-join widening.
- Bounds conversation-kind, channel, user, and legacy dynamic-join state; directory traversal is paginated with cursor-loop and workspace-size guards.
- Implements `reactionNotifications` (`off | own | all | allowlist`) on the same policy authority. Reaction allowlists are exact Slack reaction names; malformed, numeric, empty, or dangling allowlists fail startup.
- Bridges authorized adds to `EventType.REACTION_RECEIVED`; removals stay plugin-local because core defines no removal contract. Missing `item.type`/`event_ts`, self loops, unauthorized users/DMs/workspaces, unknown lanes, and ambiguous lanes fail closed.
- Persists each outbound Slack response under its returned account/channel/message timestamp and actual thread room, including chunked responses, so `own` reaction targets can be resolved without `Date.now()` identity.
- Reports and rethrows policy, database, and event-emission failures. This is observability, not a retry guarantee: Bolt automatically acknowledges Events API events.
- Rejects accepted security-relevant configuration that the connector cannot enforce instead of silently ignoring it.

## #17469 / #17470 integration decision

- **#17469:** its useful reaction bridge is consolidated here, but not its fallback identity/room behavior. This head does not swallow DB/API errors, does not fabricate `Date.now()` event IDs, requires `item.type === "message"`, and applies full workspace/conversation/user/reaction policy.
- **#17470:** only fail-closed workspace isolation is integrated. Its process-local dedupe/arbitration and private Bolt reconnect hook are not imported. Exact review found retries could be dropped after failed processing, late mentions could double-dispatch, state was not replica/restart safe, missing workspace identity failed open, and the reconnect hook could silently disappear.
- Reliable dedupe/arbitration still requires a durable inbox persisted before acknowledgement through a supported custom receiver, with atomic account/workspace claims and worker/outbox processing. This draft does not claim that architecture exists.

7a:T2971,## Summary

- carry the bot-issued opaque Telegram continuation through provider authentication without trusting browser-supplied Telegram identity
- verify Telegram HMAC/freshness, resolve the prospective account read-only, and acquire an exclusive continuation claim before Telegram or phone mutation
- bind claim, redemption, replay, and completion to the canonical user, organization, Telegram identity, mode, and normalized phone
- make same-identity retries idempotent while rejecting concurrent, stale, cross-account, cross-org, cross-Telegram, and cross-phone attempts
- make an interrupted attempt recoverable: the exact claim holder resumes its own claim after a transient redemption/completion failure, and a leftover claim on a canonically bound session settles into idempotent completed replays
- link the Telegram and phone identity pair atomically across the canonical `users` row and the `user_identities` projection that auth lookups read, with canonical fallback lookups so a stale or absent projection cannot strand an account
- return to Telegram only when the backend authoritatively reports `continuation_redeemed: true`

Closes #17888

## Security invariants

- browser input cannot activate trusted-Telegram mode or assert Telegram identity
- the opaque continuation is excluded from Telegram HMAC verification input
- no durable Telegram or phone mutation occurs before exclusive claim acquisition — including plain session-based linking, which validates phone bindings before the Telegram link
- claim ownership persists through identity mutation and canonical session binding until explicit completion
- elapsed time alone never transfers mutation authority; the exact claim holder (same deterministic claim id, compatible Telegram/phone/account bindings) resumes, while competing claimants receive `409`
- claim lineage is derived from the opaque token, signed Telegram id, and normalized phone — the anonymous first attempt and its post-account-creation retry share one lineage, and the account is bound to the claim record the moment it is known
- the combined Telegram+phone link commits the canonical `users` row and the `user_identities` projection as one transaction; a unique-value collision in either table aborts both writes, so neither table can retain a half-link
- account-bound observation cannot clear another request's active claim
- replay-cache presence is not authorization and signed identity is revalidated before replay
- phone-link failure, phone mismatch, partial user/org binding, or malformed successful claim JSON fail closed

## Review follow-ups

Current stack: `9a79c01be` (original) → `cc873f030` (claim resumability) → `ed887a0f1` (atomic identity linking) → `84a4bc0b8` (e2e bot-id fixture) → `ec48c139c` (landing composer test budget) → `d5acbd5df` (identity projection atomicity) → `34ca68a1c` (projection boundary consolidated) → `506ad2cc5` (verified-phone guard + typed link boundary) → `cc591dbf8` (gateway router stale-identity transition guard).

**First blocking review (claim-holder deadlock) — addressed in `cc873f030`:**

- `claimContinuation` resumes the exact holder (same claim id + compatible bindings) instead of `409`; competing claim ids and mismatched Telegram/phone/account bindings remain `409`
- a leftover claim on a canonically bound session is cleared by its own lineage and settles into completed replays, covering a crash between redemption and completion
- `createContinuationClaimId` drops account material so the anonymous create-then-retry transition hashes to the same lineage; the claim record itself carries the account binding once known
- the write-only `expiresAt` lease field is removed; time-based takeover remains impossible in both directions (pinned against legacy records still carrying the field)
- plain session-based linking validates phone bindings before any durable link; the strict-continuation identity assertion no longer early-outs for trusted transports; the redemption idempotency key includes the continuation token
- integrated regression composes the real auth route with the real coordinator Durable Objects: transient redemption failure → identical signed retry redeems exactly once; anonymous create-then-retry resumes with a stable claim id; crash between redemption and completion resolves without re-redeeming

**Second blocking review (stale `user_identities` projection) — addressed in `d5acbd5df`, consolidated in `34ca68a1c`:**

- `usersRepository.linkTelegramAndPhoneIdentity` commits the canonical `users` update and an authoritative `user_identities` upsert in ONE transaction; the projection mirrors the freshly returned canonical row, a missing projection row is inserted, and a unique collision in either table rolls back both — neither table can retain a half-link
- `linkTelegramAndPhoneToUser` routes through that boundary (the service-level test proves no separate canonical update is issued around it)
- direct auth/routing lookups remain projection-authoritative; the write-side upsert (rather than read-side fallbacks) is what prevents drift from stranding an account into the create-collide-500 chain
- repository-level regression against the real Drizzle schema (`pushSchema` on isolated PGlite): (1) link then fresh lookups resolve the user by both Telegram ID and phone; (2) a stale cross-user projection collision rolls the canonical write back with no half-link in either table; (3) a legacy user without a projection row gets one created by the link

# Summary

Migrates **Settings → Connectors** from inline accordions to a dense index/detail workflow:

- Grouped connector index with a persisted **Delegate / Bot** identity lens.
- Per-connector routes at `#connectors/<id>` with browser/hardware Back support.
- Connector enable/load switch first; duplicate schema-level `Enabled` fields are hidden.
- One config item per row.
- Text, number, secret, JSON, array, code, and multiline values rest as value chips and open a **Save / Cancel** dialog.
- Dialog Save stages edits locally; **Save changes / Cancel** commits or discards the complete bundle atomically.
- Signal and WhatsApp QR states use the same description-left/action-right pattern as other connectors.
- Required fields use badges without decorative left bars.
- Stronger contrast for primary/disabled CTAs, neutral actions, and value chips.
- Deep links and programmatic connector focus remain supported.

# Identity classification

Declared setup modes are filtered by identity. Plugin-managed inventories are filtered from each stored account record—not the catalog creation default:

- `OWNER` → Delegate
- `AGENT` → Bot
- `TEAM` or unknown role → visible in both lenses

| Connector | Delegate | Bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discord | Desktop App | OAuth Gateway, Bot Token |
| Telegram | Personal Account; stored OWNER/TEAM accounts | Cloud Gateway, Bot Token; stored AGENT/TEAM accounts |
| Slack | Stored OWNER/TEAM accounts | OAuth App, Socket Mode; stored AGENT/TEAM accounts |
| X | OAuth, local OAuth2, developer tokens; stored OWNER/TEAM accounts | Stored AGENT/TEAM accounts |
| Signal | QR-linked account; stored OWNER/TEAM accounts | Stored AGENT/TEAM accounts |
| WhatsApp | QR-linked personal account; stored OWNER/TEAM accounts | Business Cloud API; stored AGENT/TEAM accounts |
| iMessage | iPhone gateway, direct chat.db, BlueBubbles | Blooio cloud number |
| BlueBubbles | Cloud and local owner bridge | — |

Single-form fallback classifications:

- **Bot:** Bluesky, Farcaster, Nostr, Matrix, MS Teams, Mattermost, Google Chat, Feishu, LINE, Zalo Official, Tlon, Nextcloud Talk, Twitch, Blooio.
- **Delegate:** Instagram, Zalo User, Google Workspace.
- Unknown third-party connectors intentionally remain visible in both lenses.

## Known identity ambiguities

The following plugins do not declare account ownership strongly enough to classify every credential with certainty:

- Slack Socket Mode still includes optional `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` in an otherwise bot-oriented schema.
- Tlon credentials can represent an agent ship or the owner’s ship.
- Matrix credentials can represent a dedicated bot user or an owner account.
- Instagram supports personal, brand, and bot-like profiles.
- Bluesky app passwords can technically belong to either identity.
- X OAuth2 and OAuth1 modes remain one same-lens schema; this is setup-mode leakage, not a Delegate/Bot error.

# Review fixes included

- Atomic bundle save prevents overlapping plugin restarts and stale-completion draft loss.
- Failed saves retain drafts; duplicate Save clicks are ignored.
- Configured secrets cannot be deleted by empty Save/Enter.
- Optional secrets retain an explicit confirmed **Clear → Clear value** path.
- Masked secret chips have distinct accessible names (`Edit <field>`).
- User-opened detail routes use `pushState`; visible Back consumes that entry. Programmatic/deep-linked details retain replace semantics.
- Default-backed iMessage policy controls no longer require optional CLI/database path overrides.
- Mixed plugin-managed OWNER/AGENT records are separated by actual stored role; TEAM/unknown remain neutral.
- Programmatic detail→detail focus preserves the user-pushed history marker so visible Back then hardware Back leave the connectors stack cleanly.
- Catalog-backed detail modes follow the same `connectorSupportsChannelMode` lens policy as the index (e.g. Google under Bot does not expose plugin-managed inventory).
- Mobile detail hides the in-content Back control; ViewHeader remains the sole mobile Back target (`hidden` / `md:inline-flex`, `min-h-11`).

# Risks

This is a high-sensitivity connector identity change. A credential rotation must not leave autonomous work, feed attribution, prompt identity, or cursor state attached to the prior X account. The refactor keeps #20087's counted per-operation authentication leases, rejects stale generations before side effects or cache writes, partitions state by connector account plus immutable X profile ID, and publishes legacy singleton identity only for the default account.

The original draft also bundled process-local action-settlement tombstones. Those are deliberately excluded: they lacked a distributed CAS and could either duplicate across replicas or silently lose work after a crash between tombstone creation and provider egress.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Synchronizes `ClientBase` identity from the active authenticated credential generation and clears compatibility identity on refresh failure.
- Partitions timelines, mentions, recent-post history, and interaction cursors by configured account plus immutable X profile ID, with bounded migration from eligible legacy username keys.
- Prevents secondary accounts from overwriting the agent's legacy singleton entity identity.
- Carries fresh profiles through post, discovery, interaction, timeline, feed, search, and identity-provider paths.
- Marks own-post memories from the admitted profile ID rather than a startup snapshot.
- Preserves #20087's per-`next()` streaming lease behavior and trusted post/DM account routing.
- Excludes the unsafe action-settlement implementation and its claims.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix and security hardening for managed X credential rotation and multi-account attribution.

# Documentation changes needed?

Package-local `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` remain byte-identical and document credential-aware identity refresh.

# Risks

Medium. This changes authentication concurrency, makes every public X client I/O method hold a counted credential-generation lease, and binds production DM reads and writes to the captured current identity. A mistake could block credential rotation or let an old account finish work after a replacement. The adversarial tests cover concurrent initialization, tuple/mode rotation, ABA, detached async contexts, logout/replacement races, secret-bearing failures, and delayed public reads/writes.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

This is the reviewed authentication and direct-message security slice extracted from #20035:

- fingerprints the complete effective OAuth tuple without persisting or logging credential values;
- invalidates cached identity before a changed tuple can be reused;
- serializes generation admission while draining already-admitted operations;
- keeps awaited nested work pinned and prevents detached async contexts from retaining an expired account;
- makes public Client reads, writes, pagination, generators, media, and DMs hold one authenticated lease;
- fails public authentication closed and normalizes provider receipt IDs;
- deprecates raw client/session escape hatches without removing them;
- streams paginated public generators one provider step at a time and aborts between pages after rotation;
- binds live DM polling, current-profile filtering, recipient resolution, participant/conversation sends, and history reads to one authenticated session.

It intentionally excludes broader ClientBase legacy-entity and non-DM cursor partitioning plus autonomous interaction/settlement slices. It relates to #19968 but does not close it.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix / security hardening.

# Documentation changes needed?

No public setup or configuration changes. The existing package guide already describes broker, OAuth1, and OAuth2 modes; this slice changes their runtime safety contract and carries caller-facing JSDoc on the affected APIs.

<details>
<summary>Exact credential-generation domain receipt</summary>

```text
A -> B with the same access token and a changed OAuth1 secret: the client rebuilds and profile A is invalidated before B can publish.
A -> B -> C while initialization is in flight: coalesced waiters resolve C, the intermediate B profile never publishes, and the callback is not replayed.
A detached async child resumed after its A lease ends: it resolves the current B client/profile; expired A cannot egress after replacement.
A paginated provider iterator yields immediately, closes on cancellation, and cannot fetch another stale-A page after rotation.
A DM poll or connector send paused during routing/recipient lookup aborts before X egress and leaves the durable cursor unchanged after rotation.
```

# What changed

- Preference-shaped requests route to `MODEL_SWITCH`; ambiguous requests persist one room-scoped local/cloud choice, and planner options cannot authorize a switch that the user did not request.
- Response-handler deterministic calls execute without an `ACTION_PLANNER` round trip, but only after an exact evaluator-owned action allowlist check. Remote evaluator allowlists are derived from actions owned by that same remote module.
- Rejected evaluator calls contribute none of their coordinated patch. Deterministic execution preserves the turn’s original contexts and reuses the canonical role, context, private-action, argument, account, validation, callback, lifecycle, and trajectory boundaries.
- `MODEL_SWITCH` success and expected failure outcomes are verified user-facing results on callback and callback-free transports, with single-delivery behavior.
- Text routing is owned by one cross-process filesystem transaction: strict persisted-state parsing, bounded `O_EXCL` lock acquisition, dead/malformed stale-lock recovery, token-owned release, unique `0600` temp file, and atomic rename.
- One authenticated `/api/local-inference/routing/text` write publishes provider plus manual policy for both text slots. Local activation/download admission completes before routing becomes visible; a rejected activation does not alter routing.
- All official local-inference writers now use the canonical transaction rather than duplicate read/copy/write implementations.

No frontend, Cloud, billing, connector, database-schema, wallet, or deployment contract changed.

82:T9c4,## What

Adds `@elizaos/plugin-taskmarket` — lets an Eliza agent delegate a request to an external worker paid in USDC on Base ([TaskMarket](https://taskmarket.dev/)) instead of spending more inference on work another worker can do.

Three actions:

| Action | Spends? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `TASKMARKET_BROWSE` | no | list / get open tasks |
| `TASKMARKET_STATUS` | no | balance, reputation, own submissions |
| `TASKMARKET_CREATE_TASK` | **yes** | post a task (escrows real USDC) |

## Safety

`TASKMARKET_CREATE_TASK` is the only money-moving action, gated three independent ways:

1. `TASKMARKET_ALLOW_TASK_CREATION` — off by default.
2. `TASKMARKET_MAX_TASK_REWARD_USDC` — enforced **by refusal**, never by silently trimming the reward. Hard-capped at 50.
3. `userConfirmed` — must come from direct user approval, not from model-generated content.

The disabled check is duplicated in `validate()` and at handler entry on purpose: `validate()` keeps the tool off the planner's list, the handler check is the backstop against a hallucinated call. Every guard failure returns **before** the network call — the tests assert `fetch` was never invoked on each rejection path.

No action accepts a submission or releases escrow. Settlement stays with the human. Error text never echoes the bearer token or the request URL (which carries the caller's address).

## Notes from integrating against the live API

- The `/api` base-path prefix is mandatory; every path 404s without it.
- The bearer token does **not** identify the caller — account routes need an explicit `address` query param, hence the separate required `TASKMARKET_ADDRESS` setting.
- Amounts are atomic 6-decimal USDC everywhere except `/wallet/balance`. Converted at the client boundary; actions speak whole USDC.
- Task descriptions run 2–10 KB, so list output truncates (`TASKMARKET_LIST_DESCRIPTION_CHARS`) to keep a full board listing from eating the context window.

## Testing

```
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-taskmarket test        # 16 passed
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-taskmarket typecheck   # no errors in this package
```

Unit tests mock `fetch`, which validates this plugin's logic but not the vendor's URL shape — so it was also verified with a **read-only live run** against `api.taskmarket.dev` (balance, task list, task detail, submissions), plus live confirmation that all three creation guards refuse before any POST. Task creation itself is never exercised in tests; it escrows real funds.

# Risks

Medium. Changes managed X authentication initialization and adds an inbound DM polling loop. Posting, autonomous actions, and discovery remain disabled by default. First startup records the current DM watermark so old conversations are not replayed.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Single-commit landing of #19464 with the review blockers repaired and the one-off production ops tooling stripped:

- Restores the Eliza Cloud broker auth provider (`TWITTER_AUTH_MODE=broker`, OAuth 1.0a or OAuth 2.0 vended credentials) and adds an idempotent inbound DM polling loop that routes new X DMs through the agent message service and replies in the same conversation.
- **DM pagination (review blocker):** each poll pages the DM event timeline until it reaches the durable cursor (continues until the durable cursor, with a 1,000-page fail-closed guard that never advances past unseen events), so bursts larger than one 50-event page are not silently dropped.
- **Delivery settlement (review blocker):** reply delivery is tracked with a per-event settlement marker separate from inbound-memory existence; an explicit 4xx rejection is retryable, while an acceptance-unknown transport failure retains a durable no-replay tombstone because X provides no DM idempotency key.
- **Token rotation (review blocker):** the broker OAuth2 path carries an `expires_at`/refresh-rotate contract — the Cloud token route refreshes expired (or expiry-unknown) tokens against X, rotates the stored secrets, and vends `expires_at`; the plugin provider honors `expires_at` and caps its cache TTL so broker-side rotation propagates without a restart.
- Folds in the author's follow-up ownership fixes from the original branch: inbound DMs and mentions persist the canonical entity UUID as the X world owner via `reconcileTwitterWorld` (upsert on legacy runtimes), and DM connections use canonical user ids.
- **Not included, deliberately:** the production canary job and DB-surgery scripts from the original branch (`.github/workflows/test.yml` x-agent-rollout job, `x-agent-diagnostic.yml`, `.github/scripts/x-identity-hotfix-deploy.sh`, hardcoded production agent ids in `agent-image-canary-live.ts`). Those are one-off operator incident tooling and must not enter `develop`. Only the durable connector and runtime-restore changes land.

Bug fix plus non-breaking connector improvement.

# Risks

**Medium.** This touches macOS permission probing, Electrobun signing for dev/direct/MAS/updater/template builds, and the shared permission UI. The main risks are assigning the app identity too broadly, regressing Windows/Linux notification fallback, or confusing native errors with user denial. The implementation restricts identity rewriting to the top-level `Contents/MacOS/bun`, verifies it in every shipping path, retains renderer authority off native macOS, and has focused cross-platform tests.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

The actual macOS notification caller is Electrobun's packaged Bun process. It was signed as `bun` while requesting authorization for `ai.elizaos.app`, so `usernotificationsd` rejected registration before a valid prompt and the UI reported a false denial.

This PR:

- signs and verifies the actual top-level Bun permission host as the app identity across local dev, direct release, MAS, updater, and generated-project paths without adding Apple-private entitlements;
- uses stable designated requirements and the canonical `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` entitlement;
- distinguishes native request/configuration errors from real user denial;
- routes Open Settings through native RPC, checks the exact permission freshly after returning, and renders request/recheck failures explicitly;
- preserves browser notification fallback on Windows/Linux and non-Electrobun macOS;
- fixes the one-line current-develop cold-launch blocker by using Electrobun's declared local logger in the shell sync relay.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking).

# Documentation changes needed?

No end-user documentation change is required. The project scaffold and package contracts are updated so newly generated desktop apps inherit the fixed signing/entitlement behavior.

# Risks

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Splits cloud surface registration so anonymous `/login` no longer static-imports the private console module graph:

1. `registerPublicCloudSurfaces()` — join + public pages via `./public-pages/register` and `./join/register` (not fat barrels that eagerly re-export `LoginPage`).
2. `registerPrivateCloudSurfaces()` — dashboard/settings/admin via dynamic `import()` after first paint path.
3. Web shell boot calls public first, then fires private registration in the background.
4. `CloudRouterShell` subscribes to route-registry mutations so late private routes appear without a full remount.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix / performance improvement (non-breaking for hosts that already use the public registration hook; `registerAllCloudSurfaces` is now async).

89:T1703,## Problem

Settings → Models & Providers could not truthfully answer either of the two questions a user actually has, because it collapsed two independent axes into one "Cloud vs Local" bit.

**1. It reported a configured route as if it were a live one.** The cloud-proxy branch of `detectRuntimeModel` reported `elizacloud` whenever cloud-proxy was configured — with no signed-in account and no registered Cloud handler. An unsigned install showed Eliza Cloud as **Active** while every reply was in fact computed locally.

**2. It never said where the agent process runs.** The tiles only ever answered "who computes chat replies?", so these were indistinguishable:

| True state | What the tiles showed |
| --- | --- |
| Local runtime + local inference | Local **Active** |
| Local runtime + Cloud inference | Cloud **Active** |
| Hosted Cloud runtime + Cloud inference | Cloud **Active** — same as the row above |
| Hosted Cloud runtime + local inference | not modelled |

Cloud Overview compounded it, collapsing account session, runtime, and inference into "Cloud is connected" vs "Local mode is active" from `elizaCloudConnected` alone.

## Change

**Live inference source.** Cloud-proxy reports `elizacloud` only when a real `elizaOSCloud` `TEXT_SMALL` handler is registered. `resolveActiveChat` takes the runtime and omits `activeChat` when unsigned. Tiles separate serving (`current` → orange + `aria-current`) from inspecting (`selected` → quiet border + `aria-pressed`). The unsigned Cloud panel offers interactive **Sign in** instead of a no-op "Use Eliza Cloud"; Local gains a fallback banner. Model dropdowns no longer lock to Eliza Cloud unless connected.

**Two axes.** New `resolveServingAxes` classifies runtime and inference independently, rendered as a labelled **Agent runtime** / **Chat inference** row pair above the tiles. The runtime axis prefers `deploymentRuntime` from `GET /api/runtime/mode` — the server's view of the persisted `deploymentTarget.runtime`, which already records hybrid as `local` — falling back to the startup-coordinator target and first-run/mobile pins while unresolved.

`cloud-hybrid` / `elizacloud-hybrid` stay **local runtime + cloud inference**; a remote backend stays distinct from Cloud. The tiles remain the inference picker, so orange + **Active** still marks only the source actually answering chat. Cloud Overview now speaks about the account and points at Models & Providers.

Verified live in `/Applications/Eliza-dev.app` against a freshly synced renderer (`sync-desktop-renderer.mjs`), running on an isolated state dir so the existing install was untouched.

```json
{"state":"running","model":"elizacloud","cloud":{"connectionStatus":"disconnected"}}
```

That is exactly the previously-dishonest case: cloud-proxy configured, account signed out. Settings now renders:

- **Agent runtime → This device** — "The agent process runs on this device, so it stops when the app does."
- **Chat inference → This device** — "Eliza Cloud is selected but not signed in, so chat replies are computed locally until you sign in."
- Tiles: Eliza Cloud *Not signed in* (quiet) · Local provider **Active** (orange)
- Local panel banner: "Answering chat because Eliza Cloud isn't signed in."

Before this PR the same state rendered Eliza Cloud as **Active** with no runtime row at all.

# Risks

**Medium — production deploy topology only.** Dropping the shared workflow-level production group without a post-approval mutate lock would allow overlapping production mutations. This PR does not do that.

- Admission is per `run_id` (PRs still share `pr-{number}` and cancel in progress).
- `authorize-production` waits on `environment: production` with **no** mutation lock.
- `release` takes one `cloud-cf-release-v6-${env}` group (`cancel-in-progress: false`, `queue: max`) and `uses` `.github/workflows/cloud-cf-release.yml` for migrate + API + Pages + routing proof. That callee has no workflow-level or per-leg concurrency group.
- AASA CDN `--apple-cdn-live` stays inside the publish job. Provisioning SSH stays one locked job.

No Worker, Pages, Hetzner, secret, or janitor behavior changes beyond carrying #19128's Telegram bot pins into the extracted Pages build. A leftover `cloud-cf-deploy-v4/v5` waiter is orphaned by the `v6` suffix and can be cancelled by an operator.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Production acquired the shared workflow concurrency group **before any job exists**, so a waiting `environment: production` holder blocked newer canonical `main` at workflow `pending` / zero jobs (#18092). Staging already admitted before taking a shared lock.

This copies that topology and implements Shaw's review of the first head:

1. **Non-PR admission is per run, not per SHA.** Two dispatches/reruns of the same commit get distinct groups and both create jobs. PRs still supersede by number.
2. **One post-approval critical section.** `authorize-production` does not share a mutation group. `release` holds one lock across migrate, API, Pages, and routing proof. Run B cannot migrate while run A deploys API.
3. **Official GitHub queue contract.** `cancel-in-progress: false` is not a FIFO queue. Mutation locks set `queue: max` so additional approved releases wait (up to 100) instead of the default one-pending eviction. FIFO is by wait-start, not dispatch; ordering is not guaranteed. `queue: max` is not combined with `cancel-in-progress: true` (workflow validation error).

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (CI / deploy admission topology). No product runtime change.

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation. The reasoning lives in the workflow comments and the contract test.

Fixes #18054.

Anonymous navigation to `/auth/success` no longer renders a trusted "Connected" card from query parameters alone.

**Verification contract (this head `084b5512549b7d1a632dc00c8b8d786bfb199035`):**

1. Query parsing yields only a *candidate* (`resolveAuthSuccessCandidate`). Known-provider `*_connected` markers or `connection_id` alone never claim success.
2. Success requires **one** of:
   - A **callback-minted short-lived HMAC proof** verified by public `GET /api/v1/oauth/success-proof/verify?proof=…` (covers Twitter/Discord and sessionless API-key OAuth returns to `/auth/success`), and when a `connection_id` is present a sessioned browser must also own that connection; or
   - An **authenticated ownership lookup** `GET /api/v1/oauth/connections/:id` returning an active connection for the current org/user (sessioned browsers without a proof).
3. Until verification succeeds the page stays **pending**, then **verified**, **unverified**, or **unavailable** (distinct UI for transport/5xx).

**Backend changes:**

- `mintOAuthSuccessProof` / `verifyOAuthSuccessProof` (HMAC, ~10 min TTL, nonce) in cloud shared OAuth services
- Generic OAuth2, Twitter (OAuth1a + OAuth2), and Discord callbacks attach `proof` only when the redirect path is exactly `/auth/success`
- Public path allowlist for `/api/v1/oauth/success-proof/verify`
- Reserved markers (`proof`, `platform`, `connection_id`, known `*_connected`) are cleared before rewriting so a prior success URL cannot retain a valid proof across an error redirect

**Provider contracts preserved:**

| Callback | Success query shape on `/auth/success` |
| --- | --- |
| Generic OAuth2 | `{platform}_connected=true&platform=…&connection_id=…&proof=…` |
| Twitter | `twitter_connected=true&platform=twitter&proof=…` (no connection_id) |
| Discord | `discord=connected&platform=discord&discord_connected=true&proof=…` |

Forged marker-only URLs stay **unverified**.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Makes initialize, fail, cancel, settle, and expire explicit transactional state transitions with allowed-state/deadline guards and durable events emitted from the returned row. Concurrent terminal transitions cannot produce mixed status/settlement payloads.
- Preserves deliberate same-transition idempotency while rejecting conflicting replays with the current state, including initialization payload conflicts.
- Deletes the generic status-writing path: ordinary payment-request updates are structurally limited to mutable intent fields.
- Fails closed for overdue public requests, expires them from an authenticated scheduled route, and binds Stripe/OxaPay checkout lifetimes to the application deadline.
- Persists Stripe webhook settlement before dedupe/publication so failed or late callbacks retry safely and cannot credit an expired request.
- Isolates payment-page route generations, tracks the live deadline, revalidates authoritative state immediately before redirect, and renders provider labels instead of storage enum strings.
- Verifies the anonymous public contract across real auth middleware, detail route, service, repository, and PGlite. The exact eight-field serialized fixture returned there is consumed by a mounted `PaymentRequestPage` test, joining the DTO-to-hosted-page seam without claiming a live-deployment browser E2E.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking payment-integrity and checkout-navigation repair).

# Risks

Medium. This changes proactive-message delivery and retry classification across Shared scheduling, Discord, and Blooio/iMessage. The main risks are duplicate messages after ambiguous provider acceptance, permanently stranded stale claims, and false success without a durable provider receipt. The implementation uses bounded stale-claim recovery, persists and reuses the occurrence idempotency key, distinguishes known provider rejection from unknown acceptance, and fires only after a strictly validated receipt.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Extends the canonical Shared reminder destination from Telegram-only to a server-owned discriminated private-DM contract for Telegram, Blooio/iMessage, and Discord.
- Keeps the canonical scheduler and Cloudflare cron/CAS path; only the existing provider-owned gateway is selected at egress.
- Persists an occurrence-level dispatch idempotency key and reuses it across retries and stale-claim recovery.
- Adds bounded recovery for stale unsettled scheduler claims rather than leaving them permanently stranded.
- Classifies webhook Redis failures before provider egress as retryable/not accepted and keeps claim-release failures from masking the provider result.
- Separates Discord known rejection from acceptance ambiguity; ambiguous sends retain their cursor/lease and are not blindly resent.
- Requires durable provider receipts and validates connector envelopes before recording a reminder as fired.
- Enforces the connector-safe 2,000-character reminder bound at creation and defensively at dispatch.
- Commits names-only rollout/config contracts for `GATEWAY_INTERNAL_SECRET`; no secret values are read or committed.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature plus correctness hardening for a non-breaking Shared reminder delivery surface.

# Documentation changes needed?

No user-facing documentation change is required. The canonical scheduling and connector ownership contracts remain unchanged.

# Risks

Medium. This changes production backup schema and the managed-agent delete transaction. The material risks are retaining the wrong generation, deleting without recoverable state, crossing a tenant boundary, leaking offloaded payloads, or wedging cleanup behind one poison row.

The implementation reuses the canonical encrypted backup table and object namespace. Capture and no-snapshot waiver state are fenced to the exact bridge/lifecycle generation; retained rows are revalidated under the lifecycle lock and at commit; allocation release returns the post-trigger revision used by the final delete CAS; lookup remains organization-scoped; and cleanup isolates each candidate while deleting external bytes before metadata.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Retains the exact final full `pre-delete` backup for 30 days after a successful managed-agent deletion instead of losing it to `ON DELETE CASCADE`. It adds explicit organization, deleted-agent, deletion-attempt, and expiry metadata; leaves ordinary backups attached so they still cascade; keeps retained rows visible to restorability verification; and cleans expired inline and R2/S3 payloads in bounded provisioning-worker batches.

The reviewed repair also:

- writes deletion intent before persisting the fresh capture, so the retained-backup timestamp predicate accepts it;
- propagates every lifecycle-trigger revision through backup persistence, allocation release, and the final row-delete CAS;
- binds the supported legacy-image no-snapshot waiver to deletion attempt, environment revision, sandbox ID, and the current bridge URL;
- makes migration constraints safe when the provisioning worker's schema ensure runs before migration;
- prevents a failed R2 candidate from starving later expired rows and accounts for terminal missing-key rows;
- adds real PGlite coverage for stale revision refusal, post-trigger deletion, timestamp boundaries, and ensure-before-migrate replay.

The cleanup/migration hardening originated in [synapz-org/eliza#1](https://github.com/synapz-org/eliza/pull/1) by `hermesagent270-commits`; it was statically audited, incorporated, and refined for the repository error policy and log redaction.

## Why this approach?

The repository already owns one backup row model, KMS path, R2 namespace, verifier, and cleanup boundary. Extending those contracts is cleaner and safer than introducing a parallel pre-deletion table or object store.

# Documentation changes

`packages/cloud/shared/docs/agent-backup.md` documents retention, tenant ownership, the typed unsupported-generation waiver, fail-closed behavior, and cleanup order.

Addresses remaining gaps from the July 23 triage of #14874.

PRs #14821 and #15084 already fixed the primary defect (model-mediated dispatch rendering). This PR closes 3 of the 5 remaining gaps identified in the triage:

### 1. Named OptimizedPromptTask slots (gap 2)
Added `scheduled_task_dispatch` and `scheduled_task_title` to the `OptimizedPromptTask` union and `OPTIMIZED_PROMPT_TASKS` array. Each dispatch surface is now independently tunable by GEPA artifacts, mirroring the existing `reminder_dispatch` precedent.

### 2. Deterministic fallback for model-free runtimes (gap 4)
The dispatch renderer previously threw a retryable `ElizaError` when `runtime.useModel` was not a function. On a stock mobile boot (no model provider), this caused every scheduled task to fail with a retryable dispatch error instead of delivering the notification.

Now, a model-free runtime receives a **neutral intensity-keyed canned message** — never the raw `promptInstructions` text. The fallback does not consult `promptInstructions` at all; it cannot leak instruction text. This preserves the acceptance criterion: "Model-free host behavior unchanged; runner unit tests still pass with zero model deps."

### 3. OptimizedPrompt slots wired into dispatch-render prompts (gap 3)
The dispatch body and title render prompts are now resolved through `resolveOptimizedPromptForRuntime(runtime, "scheduled_task_dispatch"|"scheduled_task_title", baseline)`, so offline optimizers can swap in tuned artifacts.

# Outcome

Validated tool-call arguments still reach the selected handler byte-exact, but every diagnostic copy now passes through one composed, non-mutating projection before it reaches a model prompt, observer, context event, summary, or persistent trajectory.

The original contribution established the right primitive and covered several executor boundaries. Exact-head review found additional leaks in the next planner/evaluator model request, compaction, generic settlement reasoning, model-call persistence, summaries, rescue prompts, and repeat-correlation material. Those gaps are repaired on the contributor branch and the complete series is rebased onto current `develop`.

# Design

`packages/core/src/security/tool-diagnostics.ts` is the canonical boundary projector:

- `composeToolDiagnosticRedactor` applies runtime-known-secret redaction first, then the shared credential-shape pass for CLI credential flags, URI userinfo, authorization headers, PEM blocks, and provider-token formats.
- `projectToolDiagnosticValue` and `projectToolDiagnosticArgs` are non-mutating, cycle/depth bounded, fully mask credential-named values, preserve non-string primitives, and structurally share unchanged plain objects.
- `projectModelCallDiagnosticValue` applies the same policy to a complete model-call record without corrupting JSON Schema semantics. Schema property/definition identifiers such as `token`, `apiKey`, and `secret` remain exact so recorded requests stay replayable; descriptions, defaults, examples, tool metadata, provider options, messages, results, and actual arguments remain scrubbed.
- Operational correlation identity (`stepId`, call/run/room/message/trace ids, action identity, `llmCallId`) remains exact. Provider-attribution byte spans are dropped through the existing canonical fallback whenever projected prompt/message bytes change, so hashes and order survive without false offsets.
- Raw execution is deliberately unchanged: `trajectory.plannedQueue` retains the exact validated call and the handler receives the exact raw parameters. Redaction occurs only when a copy leaves that ephemeral execution path.

## Covered egress boundaries

| Surface | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Planner queue/context/event copies | projected at copy/emit in `planner-loop.ts` |
| Pending `onToolCallEnqueued` and streaming tool-call/tool-result observers | projected before callback/emit |
| Next planner and evaluator model history | projected structurally in `trajectoryStepsToMessages` |
| Compaction summaries and terminal messages | projected before rendering |
| Repeated-failure and sub-planner correlation | raw parameters replaced with stable SHA-256 digests |
| Action-owned summaries | projected inputs plus scrubbed summary output |
| Failure rescue/synthesis prompts | projected successful excerpts and scrubbed failed causes |
| Evaluator stream/context/stored output | projected before each egress |
| `ACTION_COMPLETED` and generic action settlement | complete payload projected, including `reasoning` and future text fields |
| Core SQL trajectory LLM/action funnels | final-write projection in `TrajectoriesService` |
| Agent SQL trajectory bridge | final-write projection in `trajectory-storage.ts` |
| JSON trajectory recorder | final-write projection for tool/model/evaluation stages |
| Provider attribution | spans invalidated whenever canonical persisted input changes |

94:T1778,# Relates to

The "fluid onboarding" spec (Shadow, cc-eliza 2026-08-11): DM the bot → tap the CTA → sign in in the browser → go back to the chat → **the agent sends the next message**. Today the last beat is missing on every platform: the gateway is request/response only, so after sign-in the DM stays silent until the user speaks again.

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

# What this does

Adds the proactive post-sign-in greeting for Discord.

**Worker (enqueue):** `runOnboardingChatWithStore` detects the exact transition where a trusted `platform:discord` session becomes account-bound by a **browser** turn (`input.authenticatedUser` present, `trustedPlatformIdentity !== true`). Bot-transport turns are excluded: on those the user just messaged and receives a synchronous reply. The greeting is server-authored (uses the captured preferred name) and enqueued best-effort — an enqueue failure logs and never fails the user's sign-in turn.

**Queue (Durable Object):** a well-known instance of the existing onboarding session coordinator (`proactive-greetings:discord`) gains `/enqueue-greeting` and `/drain-greetings` routes.
- Enqueue is keyed by session id → set semantics; a replayed/repeated authenticated turn overwrites instead of duplicating.
- Drain is atomic inside the DO's serialized fetch: claimed entries are deleted in the same operation that returns them → **at-most-once delivery**, no double-send even with multiple pollers.
- Entries older than 15 min are dropped at drain time (logged), never delivered stale.
- Greeting storage keys (`greeting:`) are namespaced away from `session:`/`history:`/`replay:`; a test pins that a real turn and a greeting in the same DO don't interfere.

**Internal route:** `POST /api/internal/discord/eliza-app/pending-greetings` (same `requireInternalAuth` as the existing messages route; router codegen re-run).

**Gateway (deliver):** the Eliza App bot **leader** polls the route every 15s (`GREETING_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`) once the bot client is ready, and sends each greeting via the bot's production DM send path (`client.users.send`). Delivery logic lives in `proactive-greeting-delivery.ts` with injected closures (same pattern as `managed-message-egress.ts`):
- 401 → refresh auth, batch skipped, nothing consumed (entries stay server-side).
- Send failure (e.g. Discord 50007 closed DMs) → terminal: the entry is claimed; re-queueing gateway-side would reintroduce the double-send class the atomic claim exists to prevent. Logged loudly.
- Poll interval cleared on leadership loss, disconnect, and shutdown.

# Bidirectional proof

- `packages/cloud/shared` test **"queues exactly one greeting when a browser turn binds a trusted discord session"** fails on develop (queue stays empty — the enqueue call does not exist) and passes with this diff. Verified by stash/run/pop.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Routes Discord DMs into the same deterministic personal Shared agent/room used by Telegram, SMS, and phone; guild traffic remains on its existing guild-scoped route.
- Resolves inbound callers to their phone-backed account and stable personal conversation instead of a random call UUID.
- Persists idempotent `call.started` and `call.ended` lifecycle events and generates the call opener through Eliza with prior cross-channel context and elapsed-time context.
- Accepts private Telegram voice notes, securely downloads and validates Ogg bytes at the credential-local gateway, transcribes them through configured Whisper, and sends the transcript through the same personal conversation.
- Repairs standalone Discord guild voice receive subscriptions, voice-state event wiring, and adds owner-authorized `/voice join|leave` controls restricted to the invoking owner's current channel.
- Updates the Cloud E2E chat assertion so server-only lifecycle events do not masquerade as visible user/assistant chat.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature plus non-breaking reliability fixes.

# Documentation changes needed?

No user-facing docs are changed in this PR. Platform limitations and deployment requirements are recorded below and in #19772.

- Payouts remain disabled; no wallet, cycle, reward, or settlement code is changed.9a:T1c0e,## Problem

A user who starts onboarding in a Discord DM with the gateway bot, taps the signup CTA, and logs in on the branded Steward (email/OAuth) surface is stranded: the web session gets a provisioned agent, but their Discord DMs stay in onboarding forever. `routeDiscordMessage` resolves DM senders exclusively via `user_identities.discord_id`, and nothing on the Steward-auth path ever wrote that row. (ONBOARDING-CANON divergence #3; designed in CTA-ELIZACLOUD-REPOINT-2026-08-07.)

Three root causes, all fixed upstream:

1. **The onboarding chat route rejected Steward sessions entirely** — it accepted only eliza-app JWTs or the internal gateway secret, so the branded login surface could not redeem a continuation token at all.
2. **No Discord branch in `maybeLinkAuthenticatedPlatformIdentity`** — phone had trusted auto-link; Discord had none.
3. **`linkDiscordToUser` wrote only the canonical `users` row** — invisible to the projection-based router even when called (the Discord OAuth session-linking path has shipped this gap since it landed).

## Fix

**Route (`onboarding/chat`):** accepts a Steward session as an authenticated browser caller — **bearer JWT only, never the steward cookie**. This POST binds sessions, links identities, and starts provisioning; Hono's `req.json()` parses cross-site `text/plain` simple requests, so a cookie-authenticated call would let an attacker holding their own continuation token drive a victim's browser into binding the attacker's Discord identity to the victim's account. The SPA transport always attaches the localStorage bearer. Steward callers are never a trusted platform transport (`trustedPlatformIdentity` stays false): they cannot mint platform-scoped sessions or claim identities from the request body — identity truth comes from the gateway-attested session plus the opaque continuation token.

**Service (`onboarding-chat`):** the identity-link step now handles `platform === "discord"` — gateway-attested identity + authenticated continuation → `linkDiscordToUser`. Exact mirror of the phone-link trust rules: `success:false` is the designed tenant-safety decline (identity owned by another account, onboarding continues); infra failures propagate and self-heal on the next eligible turn.

**Repository:** new `refreshDiscordProjectionForWrite` projects the canonical Discord fields into `user_identities` (upsert: creates a missing projection row instead of silently skipping; declines when a different user's projection owns the discord_id). `linkDiscordToUser` calls it after the canonical write **and** on idempotent re-links (healing existing canonical-only rows). `findOrCreateByDiscordId` converges canonical-only legacy links via a new `findByCanonicalDiscordIdWithOrganization` lookup instead of forking a duplicate account, and projects fresh Discord-OAuth signups.

**Cloud SPA (`/get-started`, join domain):** consumes `?onboardingSession=`, persists the opaque token across the Steward login round trip (sessionStorage+localStorage, 1h TTL, platform-scoped ids rejected — only a trusted gateway may present those), and redeems it server-side with the Steward bearer after auth. Success = "head back to your chat" + a button into `/join`. Signed-out visitors bounce to `/login?returnTo=/get-started`; the token never rides the OAuth redirect. Redemption keeps the stored token on failure for retry. The URL credential is ingested once and removed from the address bar before any login bounce; successful redemption clears both stores, and neither a rerender nor a remount can resurrect it. The POST remains single-shot via the StrictMode-safe ref and stable callback identity (the #695 failure mode).

## Bidirectional proof

The route test `accepts a Steward bearer session as an authenticated (untrusted-platform) caller` fails on develop (the route throws `Invalid Authorization header` for any non-eliza-app, non-internal bearer) and passes with this diff. The PGlite test `projects a canonical Discord link into the identity row Discord routing reads` pins the exact projection write develop never performs.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

It closes the residual acceptance gaps found after #19949:

- reports the real fixed non-eager sandbox cap separately from the funded
  eager-managed cap;
- preserves unreadable container quota sources as `unavailable` instead of a
  healthy-looking zero cap;
- makes character, app, container, and organization RPM source parsing
  fail-closed and shares the same resolvers between observation and admission;
- keeps the billing GET observation-only by reading RPM sources without
  hydrating the inference admission cache;
- rethrows unexpected implementation faults while degrading only typed source
  failures;
- adds real PGlite coverage through real session/API-key authentication,
  tenant membership, persisted counts, corrupt sources, and bigint storage;
- synchronizes the generated API router count and public SDK route inventory.

# Sync with develop\n\n- [x] Rebased onto origin/develop@131a765c3cfac15495f76eaa5f9b3c3b0e80ae63; zero conflicts and zero commits behind.\n- [x] Post-rebase verification at exact head 9d0c5991f8122c7529f29a33ad0feb093f85382e: 48 focused Bun tests passed with 118 assertions; the real POSIX watchdog self-test passed; Biome and git diff --check passed.\n\n# Risks

Medium. This changes the process-lifecycle and output-streaming behavior of the broad Cloud test runner. It preserves collect-all semantics for ordinary assertion failures and the existing Bun/PGlite status-99 normalization, while timeout, spawn, interruption, and unproven teardown states fail closed. The real Windows `taskkill /T` then `/F` behavior still requires the newly wired `windows-2025` job.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Prints the exact repo-relative manifest before each Cloud test batch starts and streams child output live.
- Replaces unbounded `spawnSync` capture with a direct-Bun asynchronous supervisor and a configurable 10-minute wall-clock deadline.
- Runs POSIX commands behind a detached supervisor that owns and pins the process group through TERM/KILL escalation. Private status/control pipes keep that anchor alive after the foreground command exits until inherited stdout/stderr drain; immutable identity and `PGID === PID` are revalidated before every group signal. Windows retains bounded `taskkill /T` then `/T /F` with spawn-time PID identity and fail-closed reuse handling.
- Retains only bounded output tails for exit classification and refuses status-99 normalization after truncation.
- Adds focused concurrency, timeout, malformed-input, signal-race, teardown, and Windows command tests.
- Adds Windows PID and POSIX process-group identity-reuse regressions proving replacements are never force-targeted, including ownership changes immediately after the supervisor is stopped and during the grace period.
- Adds real teardown regressions for both a parent that exits on TERM and a foreground command that exits 0 before timeout while a TERM-resistant descendant retains inherited pipes; the watchdog returns only after every owned process is gone.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking CI/test infrastructure hardening).

# Documentation changes needed?

No user-facing documentation change is required. The runner's optional `--batch-timeout-ms=<positive-ms>` override is self-describing and covered by its focused contract tests.

# Risks

Medium. The change migrates desktop, device-bridge, AOSP, and Capacitor loader
ownership onto the current runtime `ServiceClass` contract. It does not change
native ABI or inference algorithms, but it does affect startup and teardown on
multiple platforms. Real AgentRuntime lifecycle tests, full affected suites,
package builds/typechecks, and a strict integrated startup gate cover those
boundaries.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Replaces the removed two-argument `registerService(name, implementation)`
  calls with runtime-owned service classes.
- Gives timed ASR a stable `serviceType`, capability description, structural
  methods, and clean stop lifecycle.
- Gives each selected local-inference loader one unambiguous runtime owner and
  preserves backend-specific teardown semantics.
- Keeps registration separate from service startup so pre-initialize callers
  do not cross the runtime initialization barrier.
- Hardens tests with real `AgentRuntime` initialization, discovery, operation,
  and shutdown instead of an untyped registration mock.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking): local inference starts without `SERVICE_TYPE_MISSING`
or detached unhandled rejections.

# Documentation changes needed?

Updated the local-inference, native-inference, and Capacitor loader package
guides (and their byte-identical `AGENTS.md` copies) to document the service
ownership and lifecycle contracts.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds `@elizaos/plugin-companion`: a desktop/node WebSocket **client** so an
agent can drive an ESP32 companion device that already hosts the JSON protocol
on SoftAP (`SET_MOOD`, `GET_STATUS`, touch events). Firmware is out of tree;
this package speaks that protocol and is covered by an in-process WebSocket
stand-in so CI never needs hardware.

## What kind of change is this?

Features (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

# Documentation changes needed?

Plugin-local `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `CLAUDE.md` are included. No app or
docs-site change.

token 401, command-before-handshake, invalid mood, unknown-command, malformed
JSON, pong timeout / disconnect, missing `deviceId`.

a2:Td6e,## Problem (Shadow QA, staging.eliza.app, 2026-08-11)

> "I say hi and I just get hit with a message and the connect button. It's still not intuitive and it should engage with the user and steer them towards the connection and it should directly take them to sign in. For example I click connect and it's taking me to get started. It should take us to the login."

Repro: DM the staging Discord bot → tap **Connect** → `https://staging.eliza.app/get-started/?onboardingSession=<id>`. Because the visitor is **unauthenticated**, `get-started.tsx` has no branch for `onboardingSession && !isAuthenticated` and falls through to the SELECT_METHOD connector picker ("Anywhere you want her to be." + Telegram/iMessage/WhatsApp/Discord/Solana cards). That's backwards — they already came *from* Discord; asking them to pick a platform is a dead end.

## Fix 1 — web (`fd25d88f14`)

- New **ONBOARDING_SIGN_IN** step: `onboardingSession` + unauthenticated skips the picker and lands directly on sign-in — **Continue with Discord** primary (the continuation came from Discord), Solana wallet secondary, picker demoted to a "More ways to connect" link. Telegram continuations (`method=telegram&link=true`) keep their existing flow.
- Entry-step decision extracted to a pure function `resolveOnboardingEntryStep` (`src/lib/onboarding-continuation.ts`).
- **Deep-link integrity:** the continuation id now survives the Discord OAuth round-trip via sessionStorage (Discord's exact-match `redirect_uri` drops query params). Post-auth the existing #18161 identity-link → PROVISIONING_CHAT path receives the session id unchanged, so the DM conversation resumes.
- Solana sign-in inside a continuation resumes PROVISIONING_CHAT instead of bouncing to `/connected`.

## Fix 2 — DM conversation quality (`33afd5d38c`)

`runOnboardingChat` replies were template-only. Added a deterministic intent classifier (greeting / question / hesitation / other) over the user's latest turn with per-intent reply variants — greetings get a greeting back, questions get an answer, hesitation gets a no-pressure reassurance — and **every pre-login turn still ends on the Connect steer**. Deliberately *not* a model call: the file's existing policy (replay determinism, no cost amplification, no invented billing claims) is preserved; same input → same output.

## Bidirectional test proof

- `packages/homepage/tests/get-started-continuation-render.test.tsx` — mounts the real page in jsdom: `onboardingSession` + unauthenticated renders **sign-in, not the picker** (**fails on develop**, passes here); authenticated resume and organic-visitor picker covered as regressions.
- `packages/homepage/tests/onboarding-continuation.test.ts` — routing contract for the pure function (6 cases).
- `packages/cloud/shared/.../onboarding-chat.test.ts` — 5 new conversational cases (4 fail on develop); all 67 existing cases pass.
- Typecheck clean: `packages/homepage` (`tsc -b`), `packages/cloud/shared` (`tsc --noEmit`). Biome clean.

## Notes

- Cloud change is copy-only inside `generateOnboardingReply`/`fallbackReply` — no route, schema, session-store, or CTA-eligibility changes. The CTA/inline-URL invariant ("tap below" only when a button actually renders) is preserved and tested.
- Follow-up candidate (not in this PR): staging homepage deploy so Shadow can retest immediately.

🤖 Generated with assistance; authored and verified by 0xSolace.a3:Tded,+Fixes #16342 by making Cloud API webhook routing account-scoped and inbound processing durably idempotent.

## What changed

- Unknown or missing `metadata.phone_number_id` fails closed whenever Cloud API accounts are configured.
- Duplicate Cloud API phone-number IDs and duplicate normalized account IDs fail startup.
- Named accounts inherit policy defaults only; provider identity, transport, and credentials never leak from the default/base/env account.
- Each inbound delivery uses a distinct deterministic claim document, separate from the real inbound message ID.
- Initial acquisition uses the store's unique insert. Reclaim and terminal transitions use the adapter's atomic document compare-and-swap revision contract.
- Random lease UUIDs fence stale owners; late zombie completion fails with a typed conflict.
- Missing claim storage fails closed before connection, room, model, or Meta side effects.
- Completion/failure transition errors are propagated and reported; none are swallowed.
- If a host persisted the real message but died before completing its claim, redelivery converges on the persisted message without replaying side effects.

# Risks

Medium-high because this route can dispatch paid asynchronous jobs. Each provider attempt now has a provider-specific durable credit reservation. Only a typed, verified terminal provider verdict releases that reservation and permits fallback. Known pending jobs retain their job ID and reservation for reconciliation. A submission whose acceptance cannot be determined and has no recoverable job ID does not fall back or refund; it returns `202 submission_unknown` and settles conservatively. This is intentionally platform-safe but may charge a request whose provider-side outcome cannot be recovered.

Video attempts force the synchronous durable-reservation lane even in Workers. This adds an authoritative ledger call, but avoids a non-atomic Durable Object lease-to-database-reservation handoff for jobs that may outlive the request.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds an ordered default video chain (`fal-ai/veo3`, then Atlas-hosted `vidu/q3-turbo/text-to-video`) for requests that omit `model`. Explicit model requests remain pinned to their provider.

The maintainer repair makes fallback and settlement attempt-scoped:

- Fal and Atlas distinguish terminal rejection, known pending work, and unknown submission state.
- A fallback gets a new reservation with the fallback provider/model/billing source; the prior reservation must settle to zero first.
- Atlas poll transport errors, non-2xx responses, invalid payloads, and timeout preserve the prediction ID for the existing reconciliation sweep.
- Fal pre-enqueue transport ambiguity and Atlas submit ambiguity never dispatch a second paid provider.
- Billing, affiliate/recovery identity, generation history, defaults, and pending metadata all use the provider/model that actually ran.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix and billing-safety hardening. The request remains backward compatible: omitting `model` previously selected Fal and now selects the first configured default candidate. A new `202 submission_unknown` error state is returned when upstream acceptance cannot be determined safely.

# Documentation changes needed?

The Worker environment reference now identifies `ATLASCLOUD_API_KEY` as the Atlas image and fallback-video credential. This route has no standalone public API reference in the repository; the new response state is covered by route contract tests and the response carries a stable billing request ID.
